summary: Standing Cal Fire lookout on Greens Peak near Eagle Lake: 1948-49 predecessor, 1974 current tower, NHLR-registered 2019; usually staffed in fire season per a Peakbagging photo page dated August 6, 2002.

facts.design: Cab essentially a 732-6A design on tower plan 880-1A, the same tower plan as Fredonyer's (NHLR)

access.note: NHLR says the site is not readily accessible to the public, about 4 miles from paved road (MVT 10/91). A Peakbagging photo caption mentions a sign with visiting hours. No current access rules found.

visit.trail_note: About 4 miles from paved road (NHLR). Check with CAL FIRE Lassen-Modoc Unit before visiting.

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE), Lassen-Modoc Unit

events.note: NHLR: an earlier structure erected in 1948, later replaced. A June 30, 1948 newspaper item said a new 30-foot steel tower would probably be built on Green's Peak.

Original structure opened September 4, 1949 (NHLR and tipurdy.org). Named for Donald A. Landon. Tipurdy says it was in reality a remodeled naval tower. Conflicts with the 1948 date; see resolved_conflicts.
Lookout dedicated to Donald A. Landon, killed in action in Europe in 1944. Newspaper says the new tower was placed under construction two years earlier and completed earlier in 1952.
NHLR: the current Don Landon Lookout was constructed in 1974 and replaced the older structure erected in 1948.
June 6, 1979 Lassen County Times item: a new tower replaced a World War II airport control tower used there since the war. Conflicts with the NHLR dating; see resolved_conflicts.
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register on November 27, 2019 (US 1389, CA 212). Nominated by Brad Eells.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says a structure was erected in 1948 and the original opened September 4, 1949. A June 1948 newspaper item was a plan, not a completion. A 1952 newspaper says construction began two years before its dedication item. A 1979 newspaper says a new tower replaced a WWII airport control tower. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick one account of what stood there between 1949 and 1974.
Peakbagging calls the lookout part of the Lassen National Forest. NHLR and the record say CAL FIRE Lassen-Modoc Unit administers it. The story follows NHLR.

notes_for_editor: The record's 1974 build date and elevation (NHLR 7,145 ft = 2,178 m; record 2177.8 m) match the NHLR, so no correction is proposed. Sources disagree on the history between 1948 and 1974 (1949 opening vs 1948 erection vs 1952 dedication vs a 1979 replacement of a WWII airport control tower), and the story says so. Current staffing and access are not confirmed: the staffing line rests on a Peakbagging page with a 2002 photo, and the access level 'restricted' is my reading of the NHLR's not-readily-accessible note, not a stated rule. The CAL FIRE PDF is an undated copy hosted on a personal site. The Lassen Historical Society item on susanvillestuff.com returned 403 and was not read. Story is about 380 words including footnotes.
